paper_title: Axion Star Explosions: A New Source for Axion Indirect Detection
notes: Paper derives constraints on axion-photon coupling g_agamma from CMB optical depth measurements by Planck. The excluded region is 10^-14 GeV^-1 ≲ g_agamma ≲ 10^-10 GeV^-1 for axion masses 10^-14 eV ≲ m_a ≲ 10^-8 eV. This is an indirect detection constraint based on axion star explosions heating the intergalactic medium during the dark ages, leading to non-standard reionization. The constraint uses the 95% upper limit on Thomson optical depth τ_reio < 0.068 from Planck legacy data. Two distinct physical regimes exist: (1) patchy reionization for m_a ≲ 5×10^-13 eV where axion decay is plasma-blocked until a critical redshift, and (2) continuous reionization for m_a ≳ 5×10^-13 eV from merger-driven explosions. The paper also discusses future 21cm observations that could improve limits by an order of magnitude. The benchmark model assumes core-halo mass relation with α=2/5.
